PullRequest.Title: sessions: stop experiment overrides of the composer layout default
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Main counterpart of release PR #344647; follow-up to #344582 and #344587.

The new-session composer layout already defaults to `true`, but automatic experiment metadata still permits an assigned `false` treatment to replace that default.

- Remove only `experiment: { mode: 'auto' }` from `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout`.
- Keep the setting's default, key, scope, explicit user/workspace opt-out, and unified workspace picker prerequisite unchanged.
- Leave all neighboring experiments unchanged.
- Extend the existing composer regression assertion to require that the layout setting is not experiment-controlled.

Without this metadata, `ConfigurationDefaultOverridesContribution` does not query or apply an experiment treatment for the setting, so a cached `false` assignment cannot override its default.

## Validation

- On the release counterpart, the new assertion failed before the metadata removal (26 passing, 1 failing), then passed after it (27 passing).
- On main, the composer and configuration-default-override suites passed together: 49 passing.
  ```
  ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newSessionComposerLayout.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/services/configuration/test/browser/configurationService.test.ts --grep 'New session composer layout|ConfigurationDefaultOverridesContribution' --reporter dot
  ```
- Refreshed main's changed source outputs using the repository's incremental client transpiler.
- Targeted ESLint on both changed TypeScript files and `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check` passed.

## Manual test

In a desktop Agents Window with the unified workspace picker enabled:
1. Leave the composer setting unset and assign the old `config.sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout = false` experiment treatment. The new composer should still be enabled.
2. Set `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout` explicitly to `false` and verify the opt-out still works. Reset it and verify the new layout returns.

Manual packaged-build validation was not run.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup resolves configuration experiment defaults before restore, including the new-session composer layout setting in the base revision.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ConfigurationDefaultOverridesContribution runs at WorkbenchPhase.BlockRestore, serially scans registered properties, awaits each experiment treatment, then waits for installed extensions and reloads default configuration. The diff removes this setting from that treatment loop, so startup has one fewer awaited treatment lookup; the unchanged final default reload remains on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve TAS assignments through the shared TAS client; on cold initialization getTreatmentWithAssignment can await getTreatmentVariableAsync and the assignment service's request transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before: one logical treatment read for this setting among all experiment-controlled settings, served by the shared assignment fetch/cache. After: zero reads for this setting. The shared client fetch is not multiplied per setting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The setting's experiment metadata caused one startup treatment lookup and allowed a cached or fetched assignment to override the default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold assignment read could delay completion of BlockRestore processing; this diff removes that possible wait for this setting rather than adding one.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The cost scales with the number of experiment-controlled configuration properties. This change lowers effective cardinality by one setting on initial processing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Experimental settings are processed serially in the property loop and outer update/refetch requests are coalesced by a Throttler. The assignment service shares one TAS client and its initial fetch/cache across treatment reads; the diff does not create parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Before the diff, the setting read its treatment through the TAS client's persisted/shared assignment cache and could await the shared initial fetch on a cold cache; it was retained in autoExperimentalSettings for later refetches. After the diff it is absent from both treatment resolution and the auto-refetch set. No cache key, negative-cache state, or invalidation path is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the removed schema field is the exact gate checked before getTreatmentWithAssignment, and the contribution's startup phase, serial loop, cache-backed assignment service, and final reload are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact saved time depends on TAS cache warmth and whether another setting already causes the shared initial fetch, but the direction is non-regressive because work is removed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. The production change removes an awaited assignment lookup and retained auto-refetch membership; it does not add startup work or boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Assignment refreshes reapply automatic experiment defaults while the workbench is running.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the assignment service emits onDidRefetchAssignments, the throttled contribution reprocesses autoExperimentalSettings and pending startup settings before applying any changed defaults. The composer setting is no longer in autoExperimentalSettings, so it is off this refresh path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assignment polling/refetch occurs in the existing TAS client and then notifies configuration consumers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The shared assignment refresh boundary remains unchanged; subsequent per-setting treatment reads for this property fall from one per refresh event to zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every assignment refresh re-read this auto experiment and potentially changed the registered default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The shared refetch is asynchronous runtime work; processing this property's result previously delayed completion of the throttled configuration refresh, while the diff removes that processing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The refresh CPU/lookup cost scales with the number of automatic experimental settings. Effective cardinality decreases by one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refresh events are serialized/coalesced by the contribution Throttler. Each remaining setting is processed sequentially; this setting contributes no request after the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Before the diff, every refetch caused another treatment read for this key against the current shared TAS client and could update its registered experimental default. After the diff, no treatment or registered override is maintained for this property. Existing explicit user/workspace configuration remains handled by the normal configuration service.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: set membership and refresh call flow are explicit in the contribution implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Refresh frequency and cache-hit cost vary by session, but there is no newly introduced cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. Refresh work and retained per-setting state are reduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening or updating new-session and running-session composer UI for users who previously had a false automatic treatment.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Removing the automatic override makes the existing true default effective for those users when the unified workspace picker is enabled. On widget construction/render, the layout observable synchronously toggles CSS classes, reparents existing repository/context/tip DOM, adjusts editor spacing, and may render the already-instantiated environment picker toolbar. This is on the UI render/layout path but does not initiate session creation or remote connection.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with visible composer instances and a small fixed set of existing controls, not workspace history, repositories, messages, or remote hosts. Repository controls are moved as one container rather than rebuilt per item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The work is synchronous and scoped to each visible composer instance. Observable autoruns coalesce on source changes; there is no added promise burst, queue, or per-repository concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The layout decision is a configuration read with normal configuration caching. Cold versus warm TAS state no longer affects it. Explicit user/workspace false values still bypass the layout. No new cache or retained key is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all layout consumers were traced. The changed effective branch performs fixed-size DOM class changes/reparenting; the environment list reads registered in-memory providers, and remote host connect is only invoked after an explicit environment selection, not by enabling/rendering the layout.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of users formerly assigned false is unknown, but branch reachability is clear. The branch's bounded DOM work provides no concrete regression mechanism of reportable magnitude.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. Although the diff changes which layout some users see, it does not add heavyweight construction, boundary calls, unbounded DOM, repeated collection scans, or forced per-frame work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Running the updated composer regression test suite.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added assertions read one schema property and compare it in an existing synchronous deep equality assertion. Test execution is not a product critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant one additional object field in one test case.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No concurrency or asynchronous boundary is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The test reads the already-registered in-memory configuration schema; no cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete test diff only adds the experiment property to an existing assertion.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. The test-only allocation and comparison are constant and negligible.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. The production hunk removes automatic experiment resolution for one configuration key, reducing startup/refetch treatment work. The resulting layout branch uses bounded existing DOM and in-memory provider state with no newly introduced expensive boundary or scaling mechanism; the test change is constant-size.
